message: We’ll design for around 500 invoices a day, PDFs up to 10 MB, possible personal data, 90-day retention and Australian data processing. Let’s use Australia East as the proposed Azure location; service/model availability, backup locations and the existing accounting API’s data location remain unverified.

proposal.title: Add Australian residency, intake limits and retention
proposal.body: Preserve the existing workflow, approval controls and accounting integration. Propose Australia East (australiaeast), without recording region approval or verified availability. Interpret 10 MB as 10,000,000 bytes. Normalize approximately 500 daily uploads to 15,000 monthly intake events using a provisional 30-day planning month; this excludes retries and internal processing events. Retention implementation must cover originals and extraction audit history, with explicit backup/version cleanup qualification.

next.name: Asynchronous document intake
next.requirements: Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue. Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices. A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API. Use Azure. Recommend a coherent system and the engineering choices. Ask only a small material business question when needed; do not make me configure the system.

data.label: Upload and review in browser
data.description: Existing browser used by uploaders and reviewers; outside provisioning scope. The application authenticates staff and enforces separate upload and reviewer permissions.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Azure Container Apps, owning browser/API, background worker and isolated PDF/OCR parser. Internal generated resources include Azure Database for PostgreSQL durable queue/outbox and review state, private versioned Azure Blob Storage originals, staff sign-in, separate workload identities, regional model integration and operating tasks/monitoring. Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes; plan for approximately 500 uploads daily, with peak throughput and completion time unspecified. Treat originals and extracted fields as Confidential and potentially personal data. Extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence; incomplete or failed extraction stays visible for review. Commit workflow state and queued work transactionally; use bounded retries and recover stalled work. Bind reviewer approval to the exact result revision and delivery payload. Send with a stable operation identity; fence uncertain accounting outcomes for reconciliation rather than blindly resending. Accounting must independently pass normalized-action-v1 and durable idempotency acceptance. Keep documents and extracted data in Australia, including processing, queues, logs containing invoice data, backups and recovery copies. Australia East is proposed, not an approved region decision; verify Container Apps, PostgreSQL, Blob Storage, regional model availability, quotas, private networking and processing geography before destination selection. Do not silently use global or cross-region model processing. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days; qualify cleanup scheduling, object versions, SQL records and backup expiry rather than promise exact universal erasure. Confirm the retention start event during implementation. Keep invoice content out of routine operational logs. Parser isolation, model-service retention/abuse-monitoring policy, restore behavior and operating ownership require qualification. This diagram proves no deployment.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without recreation or modification. Receives only approved invoice payloads through an authenticated adapter. Native API mapping, durable idempotency, result lookup/reconciliation and permission scope remain unverified; the normalized contract alone does not establish compatibility. Its processing, storage, logging and backup locations are unknown and must be qualified against the Australian residency requirement before transferring extracted invoice data.

edges.label: HTTPS: upload PDF, review evidence, approve; receive status
Authenticated approved submission; stable operation ID and reconciliation

requirementDrafts.rationale: Personal invoice data could leave Australia through inference, backups, logs or the existing accounting integration unless every processing path is qualified.
requirementDrafts.basis: “they may contain personal data” and “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Keep invoice documents and extracted data within Australia across application processing, model inference, storage and data-bearing operational/recovery copies. Qualify the existing accounting destination before transfer. Explicitly flag unverified regional service/model support and prohibit silent cross-border fallback.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Cleanup must include audit records and versioned originals; backup windows can prevent immediate erasure and need explicit acceptance.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement scheduled cleanup and document deletion behavior for database records, object versions and backups; qualify the retention start event and residual recovery windows before claiming compliance.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Enforcing upload bounds protects parsing resources; daily volume informs capacity without inventing peak traffic or a processing deadline.
requirementDrafts.basis: “PDF invoices up to 10 MB, around 500 per day”
requirementDrafts.statement: Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes and plan asynchronous capacity for approximately 500 uploads per day. Reject oversized uploads explicitly before parsing. Qualify capacity with representative PDFs and retry/recovery workloads; peak arrival rate and completion-time targets remain unspecified.

decisionUpdates.sourceText: Keep documents and extracted data in Australia

skills.name: AI architecture and discovery
skills.summary: Clarify outcome, users, existing systems, data ownership and constraints. Evolve the diagram incrementally. Derive functional requirements and propose measurable quality targets as assumptions needing confirmation. Compare clouds against the actual requirements; do not assume an enterprise identity provider or a vendor. Keep proposed and accepted decisions distinct.

skills.name: Security and reliability
skills.summary: Check data classification, residency, access boundaries, encryption choices, approval of automated actions, reliability and recovery. A drawn control is not enforcement evidence. Explain missing controls and tests. Propose requirements from the components and paths; mark default targets as suggestions, never existing company policy.

skills.name: Azure architecture guidance
skills.summary: Check Microsoft 365/Entra integration only when relevant to the user. Match model, retrieval, data and runtime services to requirements. Evaluate redundancy, regional availability, identity and recovery separately. The pinned Azure reliability reference specifically covers Functions and App Service; do not extend its validation claims to other services.
